name: Wall hands battle
summary: Alone close to a wall, keep a quick volley exchange going with a compact paddle and count balls you keep in play under pace.
setup: Tape a line on the wall about 0.9 m above the floor (the net) and stand about 2.5 m from the wall
Volley continuously above the line with a short, compact stroke, paddle up in front of the chest, mixing forehand and backhand
Raise the pace for 5 volleys, then soften for 5, and repeat
Count the volleys in a row before an error (below the line, a mis-hit or a ball that gets past you). Sets of 60 s, rest 60 s
success_criterion: In 3 sets of 60 s, a best run of at least 20 volleys in a row in each set
safety_notes: Wear eye protection. High-intensity hands work: warm up first, stay at a pace you control, keep the ball below head height, and rest between sets. Stop if your wrist, elbow or shoulder hurts or if dizzy.
coach_rationale: (judgment) Errors under pressure at the kitchen line come from slow hands against fast balls (the AN-07 forced-error share); short, fast wall exchanges train a compact paddle and quick recovery. Intermediate only: pace is the point of this drill (checklist C6). Unverified coaching content until a human coach reviews the library (P15).
